NASB.1: Now in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams; and his spirit was troubled and his sleep left him.
NASB.2: Then the king gave orders to call in the magicians, the conjurers, the sorcerers and the Chaldeans to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.
NASB.3: The king said to them, 'I had a dream and my spirit is anxious to understand the dream.'
NASB.4: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: 'O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation.'
NASB.5: The king replied to the Chaldeans, 'The command from me is firm: if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be torn limb from limb and your houses will be made a rubbish heap.
NASB.6: 'But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and a reward and great honor; therefore declare to me the dream and its interpretation.'
NASB.7: They answered a second time and said, 'Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare the interpretation.'
NASB.8: The king replied, 'I know for certain that you are bargaining for time, inasmuch as you have seen that the command from me is firm,
NASB.9: that if you do not make the dream known to me, there is only one decree for you. For you have agreed together to speak lying and corrupt words before me until the situation is changed; therefore tell me the dream, that I may know that you can declare to me its interpretation.'
NASB.10: The Chaldeans answered the king and said, 'There is not a man on earth who could declare the matter for the king, inasmuch as no great king or ruler has [ever] asked anything like this of any magician, conjurer or Chaldean.
NASB.11: 'Moreover, the thing which the king demands is difficult, and there is no one else who could declare it to the king except gods, whose dwelling place is not with [mortal] flesh.'
NASB.12: Because of this the king became indignant and very furious and gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
NASB.13: So the decree went forth that the wise men should be slain; and they looked for Daniel and his friends to kill [them].
NASB.14: Then Daniel replied with discretion and discernment to Arioch, the captain of the king's bodyguard, who had gone forth to slay the wise men of Babylon;
NASB.15: he said to Arioch, the king's commander, 'For what reason is the decree from the king [so] urgent?' Then Arioch informed Daniel about the matter.
NASB.16: So Daniel went in and requested of the king that he would give him time, in order that he might declare the interpretation to the king.
NASB.17: Then Daniel went to his house and informed his friends, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, about the matter,
NASB.18: so that they might request compassion from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
NASB.19: Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven;
NASB.20: Daniel said, 'Let the name of God be blessed forever and ever, For wisdom and power belong to Him.
NASB.21: 'It is He who changes the times and the epochs; He removes kings and establishes kings; He gives wisdom to wise men And knowledge to men of understanding.
NASB.22: 'It is He who reveals the profound and hidden things; He knows what is in the darkness, And the light dwells with Him.
NASB.23: 'To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, For You have given me wisdom and power; Even now You have made known to me what we requested of You, For You have made known to us the king's matter.'
NASB.24: Therefore, Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and spoke to him as follows: 'Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon! Take me into the king's presence, and I will declare the interpretation to the king.'
NASB.25: Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel into the king's presence and spoke to him as follows: 'I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can make the interpretation known to the king!'
NASB.26: The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, 'Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen and its interpretation?'
NASB.27: Daniel answered before the king and said, 'As for the mystery about which the king has inquired, neither wise men, conjurers, magicians [nor] diviners are able to declare [it] to the king.
NASB.28: 'However, there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will take place in the latter days. This was your dream and the visions in your mind [while] on your bed.
NASB.29: 'As for you, O king, [while] on your bed your thoughts turned to what would take place in the future; and He who reveals mysteries has made known to you what will take place.
NASB.30: 'But as for me, this mystery has not been revealed to me for any wisdom residing in me more than [in] any [other] living man, but for the purpose of making the interpretation known to the king, and that you may understand the thoughts of your mind.
NASB.31: 'You, O king, were looking and behold, there was a single great statue; that statue, which was large and of extraordinary splendor, was standing in front of you, and its appearance was awesome.
NASB.32: 'The head of that statue [was made] of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,
NASB.33: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.
NASB.34: 'You continued looking until a stone was cut out without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them.
NASB.35: 'Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were crushed all at the same time and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away so that not a trace of them was found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
NASB.36: 'This [was] the dream; now we will tell its interpretation before the king.
NASB.37: 'You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the strength and the glory;
NASB.38: and wherever the sons of men dwell, [or] the beasts of the field, or the birds of the sky, He has given [them] into your hand and has caused you to rule over them all. You are the head of gold.
NASB.39: 'After you there will arise another kingdom inferior to you, then another third kingdom of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
NASB.40: 'Then there will be a fourth kingdom as strong as iron; inasmuch as iron crushes and shatters all things, so, like iron that breaks in pieces, it will crush and break all these in pieces.
NASB.41: 'In that you saw the feet and toes, partly of potter's clay and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but it will have in it the toughness of iron, inasmuch as you saw the iron mixed with common clay.
NASB.42: '[As] the toes of the feet [were] partly of iron and partly of pottery, [so] some of the kingdom will be strong and part of it will be brittle.
NASB.43: 'And in that you saw the iron mixed with common clay, they will combine with one another in the seed of men; but they will not adhere to one another, even as iron does not combine with pottery.
NASB.44: 'In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, and [that] kingdom will not be left for another people; it will crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, but it will itself endure forever.
NASB.45: 'Inasmuch as you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands and that it crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold, the great God has made known to the king what will take place in the future; so the dream is true and its interpretation is trustworthy.'
NASB.46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and did homage to Daniel, and gave orders to present to him an offering and fragrant incense.
NASB.47: The king answered Daniel and said, 'Surely your God is a God of gods and a Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, since you have been able to reveal this mystery.'
NASB.48: Then the king promoted Daniel and gave him many great gifts, and he made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.
NASB.49: And Daniel made request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego over the administration of the province of Babylon, while Daniel [was] at the king's court.

NLT.26: The king said to Daniel (also known as Belteshazzar), “Is this true? Can you tell me what my dream was and what it means?”
NLT.27: Daniel replied, “There are no wise men, enchanters, magicians, or fortune-tellers who can reveal the king’s secret.
NLT.28: But there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the future. Now I will tell you your dream and the visions you saw as you lay on your bed.
NLT.29: “While Your Majesty was sleeping, you dreamed about coming events. He who reveals secrets has shown you what is going to happen.
NLT.30: And it is not because I am wiser than anyone else that I know the secret of your dream, but because God wants you to understand what was in your heart.
NLT.31: “In your vision, Your Majesty, you saw standing before you a huge, shining statue of a man. It was a frightening sight.
NLT.32: The head of the statue was made of fine gold. Its chest and arms were silver, its belly and thighs were bronze,
NLT.33: its legs were iron, and its feet were a combination of iron and baked clay.
NLT.34: As you watched, a rock was cut from a mountain, but not by human hands. It struck the feet of iron and clay, smashing them to bits.
NLT.35: The whole statue was crushed into small pieces of iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold. Then the wind blew them away without a trace, like chaff on a threshing floor. But the rock that knocked the statue down became a great mountain that covered the whole earth.
NLT.36: “That was the dream. Now we will tell the king what it means.
NLT.37: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings. The God of heaven has given you sovereignty, power, strength, and honor.
NLT.38: He has made you the ruler over all the inhabited world and has put even the wild animals and birds under your control. You are the head of gold.
NLT.39: “But after your kingdom comes to an end, another kingdom, inferior to yours, will rise to take your place. After that kingdom has fallen, yet a third kingdom, represented by bronze, will rise to rule the world.
NLT.40: Following that kingdom, there will be a fourth one, as strong as iron. That kingdom will smash and crush all previous empires, just as iron smashes and crushes everything it strikes.
NLT.41: The feet and toes you saw were a combination of iron and baked clay, showing that this kingdom will be divided. Like iron mixed with clay, it will have some of the strength of iron.
NLT.42: But while some parts of it will be as strong as iron, other parts will be as weak as clay.
NLT.43: This mixture of iron and clay also shows that these kingdoms will try to strengthen themselves by forming alliances with each other through intermarriage. But they will not hold together, just as iron and clay do not mix.
NLT.44: “During the reigns of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed or conquered. It will crush all these kingdoms into nothingness, and it will stand forever.
NLT.45: That is the meaning of the rock cut from the mountain, though not by human hands, that crushed to pieces the statue of iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God was showing the king what will happen in the future. The dream is true, and its meaning is certain.”
NLT.46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar threw himself down before Daniel and worshiped him, and he commanded his people to offer sacrifices and burn sweet incense before him.
NLT.47: The king said to Daniel, “Truly, your God is the greatest of gods, the Lord over kings, a revealer of mysteries, for you have been able to reveal this secret.”
NLT.48: Then the king appointed Daniel to a high position and gave him many valuable gifts. He made Daniel ruler over the whole province of Babylon, as well as chief over all his wise men.
NLT.49: At Daniel’s request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be in charge of all the affairs of the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained in the king’s court.

WEB.1: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep went from him.
WEB.2: Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the enchanters, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.
WEB.3: The king said to them, I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.
WEB.4: Then spoke the Chaldeans to the king in the Syrian language, O king, live forever: tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.
WEB.5: The king answered the Chaldeans, The thing is gone from me: if you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall be cut in pieces, and your houses shall be made a dunghill.
WEB.6: But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive of me gifts and rewards and great honor: therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.
WEB.7: They answered the second time and said, Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.
WEB.8: The king answered, I know of a certainty that you would gain time, because you see the thing is gone from me.
WEB.9: But if you don’t make known to me the dream, there is but one law for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until the time be changed: therefore tell me the dream, and I shall know that you can show me its interpretation.
WEB.10: The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, There is not a man on the earth who can show the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler, has asked such a thing of any magician, or enchanter, or Chaldean.
WEB.11: It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.
WEB.12: For this cause the king was angry and very furious, and commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
WEB.13: So the decree went out, and the wise men were to be slain; and they sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.
WEB.14: Then Daniel returned answer with counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, who was gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon;
WEB.15: he answered Arioch the king’s captain, Why is the decree so urgent from the king? Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.
WEB.16: Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation.
WEB.17: Then Daniel went to his house, and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions:
WEB.18: that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his companions should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
WEB.19: Then was the secret revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
WEB.20: Daniel answered, Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for wisdom and might are his.
WEB.21: He changes the times and the seasons; he removes kings, and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding;
WEB.22: he reveals the deep and secret things; he knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.
WEB.23: I thank you, and praise you, you God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the king’s matter.
WEB.24: Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and said thus to him: Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon; bring me in before the king, and I will show to the king the interpretation.
WEB.25: Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste, and said thus to him, I have found a man of the children of the captivity of Judah, who will make known to the king the interpretation.
WEB.26: The king answered Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen, and its interpretation?
WEB.27: Daniel answered before the king, and said, The secret which the king has demanded can neither wise men, enchanters, magicians, nor soothsayers, show to the king;
WEB.28: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these:
WEB.29: as for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.
WEB.30: But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any wisdom that I have more than any living, but to the intent that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and that you may know the thoughts of your heart.
WEB.31: You, O king, saw, and behold,  a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its aspect was awesome.
WEB.32: As for this image, its head was of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of brass,
WEB.33: its legs of iron, its feet part of iron, and part of clay.
WEB.34: You saw until a stone was cut out without hands, which struck the image on its feet that were of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces.
WEB.35: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them: and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
WEB.36: This is the dream; and we will tell its interpretation before the king.
WEB.37: You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, and the strength, and the glory;
WEB.38: and wherever the children of men dwell, the animals of the field and the birds of the sky has he given into your hand, and has made you to rule over them all: you are the head of gold.
WEB.39: After you shall arise another kingdom inferior to you; and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth.
WEB.40: The fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and subdues all things; and as iron that crushes all these, shall it break in pieces and crush.
WEB.41: Whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, it shall be a divided kingdom; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, because you saw the iron mixed with miry clay.
WEB.42: As the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.
WEB.43: Whereas you saw the iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men; but they shall not cling to one another, even as iron does not mingle with clay.
WEB.44: In the days of those kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed, nor shall its sovereignty be left to another people; but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever.
WEB.45: Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what shall happen hereafter: and the dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.
WEB.46: Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, and worshiped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an offering and sweet odors to him.
WEB.47: The king answered to Daniel, and said, Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.
WEB.48: Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and made him to rule over the whole province of Babylon, and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.
WEB.49: Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, over the affairs of the province of Babylon: but Daniel was in the gate of the king.

AMP.1: In the second year (604 b.c.) of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams which troubled and disturbed his spirit and [interfered with] his ability to sleep.
AMP.2: Then the king gave a command to call the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.
AMP.3: The king said to them, "I had a dream, and my spirit is troubled and anxious to know the [content and meaning of the] dream."
AMP.4: Then the Chaldeans said to the king in Aramaic, "O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation."
AMP.5: The king replied to the Chaldeans, "My command is firm and unchangeable: if you do not reveal to me the [content of the] dream along with its interpretation, you shall be cut into pieces and your houses shall be made a heap of rubbish.
AMP.6: "But if you tell [me] the [content of the] dream along with its interpretation, you shall receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation."
AMP.7: They answered again, "Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will explain its interpretation [to you]."
AMP.8: The king replied, "I know for certain that you are bargaining for time, because you have seen that my command [to you] is firm and irrevocable.
AMP.9: If you will not reveal to me the [content of the] dream, there is but one sentence for you; for you have [already] prepared lying and corrupt words [and you have agreed together] to speak [them] before me [hoping to delay your execution] until the situation is changed. Therefore, tell me the dream [first], and then I will know [with confidence] that you can give me its interpretation."
AMP.10: The Chaldeans answered the king and said, "There is not a man on earth who can tell the king this matter, for no king, lord or ruler has ever asked such a thing as this of any magician or enchanter or Chaldean.
AMP.11: Furthermore, what the king demands is an unusual and difficult thing indeed! No one except the gods can reveal it to the king, and their dwelling is not with [mortal] flesh."
AMP.12: Because of this the king was indignant and extremely furious and gave a command to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
AMP.13: So the decree went out that the wise men were to be killed; and they looked for Daniel and his companions to put them to death.
AMP.14: Then Daniel replied with discretion and wisdom to Arioch, the captain of the king's bodyguard, who had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon;
AMP.15: he said to Arioch, the king's captain, "Why is the decree from the king so harsh and urgent?" Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
AMP.16: So Daniel went in and asked the king to appoint a date and give him time, so that he might reveal to the king the interpretation of the dream.
AMP.17: Then Daniel returned to his house and discussed the matter with Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions,
AMP.18: in order that they might seek compassion from the God of heaven regarding this secret, so that Daniel and his companions would not be executed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
AMP.19: Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.

AMP.26: The king said to Daniel, whose [Babylonian] name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to reveal to me the [content of the] dream which I have seen and its interpretation?"
AMP.27: Daniel answered the king and said, "Regarding the mystery about which the king has inquired, neither the wise men, enchanters, magicians, nor astrologers are able to answer the king,
AMP.28: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will take place in the latter days (end of days). This was your dream and the vision [that appeared] in your mind while on your bed.
AMP.29: "As for you, O king, as you were lying on your bed thoughts came into your mind about what will take place in the future; and He who reveals secrets has shown you what will occur.
AMP.30: But as for me, this secret has not been revealed to me because my wisdom is greater than that of any other living man, but in order to make the interpretation known to the king, and so that you may understand [fully] the thoughts of your mind.
AMP.31: "You, O king, were looking, and behold, [there was] a single great statue; this image, which was large and of unsurpassed splendor, stood before you, and its appearance was awesome and terrifying.
AMP.32: As for this statue, its head was made of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,
AMP.33: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay [pottery].
AMP.34: As you were looking, a stone was cut out without [human] hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them.
AMP.35: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed together and became like the chaff from the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away so that not a trace of them could be found. AMP.36: "This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.
AMP.37: You, O king, are the king of [earthly] kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the strength and the glory;
AMP.38: and wherever the sons of men dwell, and the beasts of the field, and the birds of the heavens, He has given them into your hand and has made you ruler over them all. You [king of Babylon] are the head of gold.
AMP.39: After you will arise another kingdom (Medo-Persia) inferior to you, and then a third kingdom of bronze (Greece under Alexander the Great), which will rule over all the earth.
AMP.40: Then a fourth kingdom (Rome) will be strong as iron, for iron breaks to pieces and shatters all things; and like iron which crushes things in pieces, it will break and crush all these [others].
AMP.41: And as you saw the feet and toes, partly of potter's clay and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but there will be in it some of the durability and strength of iron, just as you saw the iron mixed with common clay.
AMP.42: As the [ten] toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of clay, so some of the kingdom will be strong, and another part of it will be brittle.
AMP.43: And as you saw the iron mixed with common clay, so they will combine with one another in the seed of men; but they will not merge [for such diverse things or ideologies cannot unite], even as iron does not mix with clay.
AMP.44: In the days of those [final ten] kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will its sovereignty be left for another people; but it will crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.
AMP.45: Just as you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands and that it crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold, the great God has revealed to the king what will take place in the future; so the dream is true and its interpretation is trustworthy."
AMP.46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell face downward and paid respect to Daniel [as a great prophet of the highest God], and gave orders for an offering and fragrant incense to be presented to him [in honor of his God].
AMP.47: The king answered Daniel and said, "Most certainly your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, since you have been able to reveal this mystery!"
AMP.48: Then the king promoted Daniel [to an exalted position] and gave him many great gifts, and he made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.
AMP.49: And Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego over the affairs of the province of Babylon, while Daniel was at the court of the king.

NET.42: In that the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of clay, the latter stages of this kingdom will be partly strong and partly fragile.
NET.43: And in that you saw iron mixed with wet clay, so people will be mixed with one another without adhering to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay.
NET.44: In the days of those kings the God of heaven will raise up an everlasting kingdom that will not be destroyed and a kingdom that will not be left to another people. It will break in pieces and bring about the demise of all these kingdoms. But it will stand forever.
NET.45: You saw that a stone was cut from a mountain, but not by human hands; it smashed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold into pieces. The great God has made known to the king what will occur in the future. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is reliable.”
NET.46: Then King Nebuchadnezzar bowed down with his face to the ground and paid homage to Daniel. He gave orders to offer sacrifice and incense to him.
NET.47: The king replied to Daniel, “Certainly your God is a God of gods and Lord of kings and revealer of mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery!”
NET.48: Then the king elevated Daniel to high position and bestowed on him many marvelous gifts. He granted him authority over the entire province of Babylon and made him the main prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.
NET.49: And at Daniel’s request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the administration of the province of Babylon. Daniel himself served in the king’s court.
